## AIVDM/AIVDO Payload Armoring

The data payload is an ASCII-encoded bit vector. Each character represents six bits of data. To recover the six bits, subtract 48 from the ASCII character value; if the result is greater than 40 subtract 8. According to [\[IEC-PAS\]](https://gpsd.io/AIVDM.html#IEC-PAS), the valid ASCII characters for this encoding begin with "0" (64) and end with "w" (87); however, the intermediate range "X" (88) to "\\" (95) is not used.

Table 2. ASCII payload armoring

| Char | ASCII | Decimal | Bits   |
|------|-------|---------|--------|
| "0"  | 48    | 0       | 000000 |
| "1"  | 49    | 1       | 000001 |
| "2"  | 50    | 2       | 000010 |
| "3"  | 51    | 3       | 000011 |
| "4"  | 52    | 4       | 000100 |
| "5"  | 53    | 5       | 000101 |
| "6"  | 54    | 6       | 000110 |
| "7"  | 55    | 7       | 000111 |
| "8"  | 56    | 8       | 001000 |
| "9"  | 57    | 9       | 001001 |
| ":"  | 58    | 10      | 001010 |
| ";"  | 59    | 11      | 001011 |

| "m"  | 109   | 53      | 110101 |

Concatenate all six-bit quantities found in the payload, MSB first. This is the binary payload of the sentence.
